title: State Best Practices
description: Learn patterns and best practices for managing state effectively.

data.text: Managing state effectively is crucial for building maintainable React applications. Let's explore best practices and common patterns.
Only keep state in a component if no other component needs that data. This reduces complexity and makes components more reusable.

data.title: Local vs Shared State

data.text: When multiple components need the same state, move it to their closest common parent. This is called 'lifting state up'.

data.title: Lifting State Up

data.text: When state values always change together, consider grouping them into a single object.

data.title: Related State

data.text: Don't store values in state that can be computed from other state or props. Calculate them during render instead.

data.title: Derived Values
data.content: Calculate values instead of storing them

data.title: Single Source of Truth
data.text: Each piece of state should have one owner. If multiple components need the same data, lift it up to a common ancestor or use context.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Keep state as local as possible
Lift state up when multiple components need it
Don't store values that can be derived
data.takeaway: Good state management makes your app easier to reason about. Let's apply this to forms.
